entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6843"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 116</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.116.1-Ps.116.19">Psa 116:1-19</reference>. The writer celebrates the deliverance from extreme perils by which he was favored, and pledges grateful and pious public acknowledgments.</title> <div sID="gen10503" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6843"/>1-2. A truly grateful love will be evinced by acts of worship, which calling on God expresses (<reference osisRef="Ps.116.13">Psa 116:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.55.16">Psa 55:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.86.7">86:7</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Ps.17.6">Psa 17:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.31.2">31:2</reference>). <div eID="gen10503" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: PSALM 116 Psa 116:1-19 . The writer celebrates the deliverance from extreme perils by which he was favored, and pledges grateful and pious public acknowledgments. 1-2. A truly grateful love will be evinced by acts of worship, which calling on God expresses ( Psa 116:13 ; Psa 55:16 ; 86:7 ; compare Psa 17:6 ; 31:2 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6845"/><div sID="gen10506" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6845"/>5-8. The relief which he asked is the result not of his merit, but of God's known pity and tenderness, which is acknowledged in assuring himself (his "soul," <reference osisRef="Ps.11.1">Psa 11:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.16.10">16:10</reference>) of rest and peace. All calamities [Psa 116:8] are represented by death, tears, and falling of the feet (<reference osisRef="Ps.56.13">Psa 56:13</reference>). <div eID="gen10506" type="x-p"/>
